## How to use this

The code from Lecture 24, run, with the numbers it produces, and the coral
exercise solved.

. . .

`glm()` gives exact answers, so your numbers should match these. Lecture 21's
recipe uses random draws, so those may differ in the last decimal place.

::: {.notes}
Posted after class so nobody is left wondering whether their answer was right.
:::

## You've already fit one {.smaller}

```{r}
library(bbmle)
library(biometrydata)
occ <- bobwhite_occupancy

m_occ <- mle2(n_occupied ~ dbinom(size = n_routes, prob = plogis(a + b * elapsed)),
              start = list(a = 2, b = -0.05), data = occ)
g_occ <- glm(cbind(n_occupied, n_routes - n_occupied) ~ elapsed,
             family = binomial, data = occ)
coef(m_occ)
coef(g_occ)
c(logLik(m_occ), logLik(g_occ))
g_occ$iter      # rounds of reweighting glm() needed
```

## Coefficients and the trap {.smaller}

```{r}
plogis(coef(g_occ)[1])    # share of routes occupied in 1997
exp(coef(g_occ)[2])       # odds multiplied by this each year

# interval is ignored, and the answer is a logit
predict(g_occ, newdata = data.frame(elapsed = c(0, 22)), interval = "confidence")
plogis(predict(g_occ, newdata = data.frame(elapsed = c(0, 22))))   # the probabilities
```

## The band, the quick way {.smaller}

```{r}
p19 <- predict(g_occ, newdata = data.frame(elapsed = 22),
               type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
p19$fit
p19$se.fit
ends <- p19$fit + c(-1.96, 0, 1.96) * p19$se.fit
ends
plogis(ends)
qnorm(0.975)    # where 1.96 comes from

# Lecture 21's recipe, same seed
set.seed(21)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(1000, mu = coef(m_occ), Sigma = vcov(m_occ))
quantile(plogis(draws[, "a"] + 22 * draws[, "b"]), c(0.025, 0.975))
```

## The same band, the easy way {.smaller}

```{r}
library(marginaleffects)
predictions(g_occ, newdata = data.frame(elapsed = 22))

library(emmeans)
emmeans(g_occ, ~ elapsed, at = list(elapsed = 22), type = "response")
```

## Songbirds: set up and fit {.smaller}

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
songbirds <- avonet[avonet$Order1 == "Passeriformes", ]
birds <- data.frame(species = songbirds$Species1,
                    hwi = songbirds$Hand.Wing.Index,
                    lat = abs(songbirds$Centroid.Latitude),
                    migratory = as.numeric(songbirds$Migration == 3),
                    mass = songbirds$Mass,
                    wing = songbirds$Wing.Length)
birds <- na.omit(birds)
mean(birds$migratory)

g_lat <- glm(migratory ~ lat, family = binomial, data = birds)
g_add <- glm(migratory ~ lat + hwi, family = binomial, data = birds)
AICtab(g_lat, g_add)
coef(g_add)
```

## What the coefficients mean {.smaller}

```{r}
exp(coef(g_add)[-1])                  # odds ratios per degree and per HWI unit
exp(confint.default(g_add)[-1, ])
predict(g_add, newdata = data.frame(lat = 45, hwi = c(15, 30)), type = "response")

# for anyone fast: does wing shape matter differently by latitude?
g_int <- glm(migratory ~ lat * hwi, family = binomial, data = birds)
AICtab(g_add, g_int)
```

## Draw it {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.2
grid <- expand.grid(lat = 0:70, hwi = c(15, 30))
p <- predict(g_add, newdata = grid, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
grid$prob <- plogis(p$fit)
grid$lwr <- plogis(p$fit - 1.96 * p$se.fit)
grid$upr <- plogis(p$fit + 1.96 * p$se.fit)

ggplot(grid, aes(x = lat, y = prob, fill = factor(hwi))) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(color = factor(hwi))) +
  labs(x = "degrees from the equator", y = "probability of migrating",
       fill = "HWI", color = "HWI")
```

## The same figure, the easy way {.smaller}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.2
plot_predictions(g_add, condition = list("lat", hwi = c(15, 30))) +
  labs(x = "degrees from the equator", y = "probability of migrating")
```

## Reef fish: Poisson first {.smaller}

```{r}
reef <- reef_surveys
g_pois <- glm(richness ~ depth + I(depth^2), family = poisson, data = reef)

# share of surveys inside the Poisson's 95% range (should be about 0.95)
mu <- fitted(g_pois)
lo <- qpois(0.025, mu)
hi <- qpois(0.975, mu)
mean(reef$richness >= lo & reef$richness <= hi)
c(above = mean(reef$richness > hi), below = mean(reef$richness < lo))
```

## Reef fish: the fix {.smaller}

```{r}
g_nb <- MASS::glm.nb(richness ~ depth + I(depth^2), data = reef)
AICtab(g_pois, g_nb)

# the same range check for the negative binomial
lo_n <- qnbinom(0.025, mu = fitted(g_nb), size = g_nb$theta)
hi_n <- qnbinom(0.975, mu = fitted(g_nb), size = g_nb$theta)
mean(reef$richness >= lo_n & reef$richness <= hi_n)

# standard errors side by side
cbind(poisson = summary(g_pois)$coefficients[, 2],
      negbin = summary(g_nb)$coefficients[, 2])
-coef(g_nb)["depth"] / (2 * coef(g_nb)["I(depth^2)"])    # depth of peak richness
```

## A power law with `nls()` {.smaller}

```{r}
start_ll <- coef(lm(log(wing) ~ log(mass), data = birds))
n_wing <- nls(wing ~ a * mass^b, data = birds,
              start = list(a = exp(start_ll[[1]]), b = start_ll[[2]]))
coef(n_wing)
confint.default(n_wing)
confint(n_wing)        # profile intervals, slower

# the same model in mle2()
m_wing <- mle2(wing ~ dnorm(mean = a * mass^b, sd = s), data = birds,
               start = list(a = exp(start_ll[[1]]), b = start_ll[[2]], s = 10))
coef(m_wing)
c(logLik(n_wing), logLik(m_wing))
```

## Your turn: build the data {.smaller}

```{r}
corals <- coral_cover[coral_cover$REGION == "Tortugas", ]
corals$station <- paste(corals$PRIMARY_SAMPLE_UNIT, corals$STATION_NR, corals$YEAR)
stations <- unique(corals[, c("station", "YEAR")])

susceptible <- "Colpophyllia|Dendrogyra|Dichocoenia|Diploria|Eusmilia|Meandrina"
found_at <- corals$station[grepl(susceptible, corals$COVER_CAT_NAME)]
stations$found <- as.numeric(stations$station %in% found_at)
stations$year <- factor(stations$YEAR)

nrow(stations)
tapply(stations$found, stations$year, mean)
```

## Your turn: fit it {.smaller}

```{r}
g_null <- glm(found ~ 1, family = binomial, data = stations)
g_year <- glm(found ~ year, family = binomial, data = stations)
AICtab(g_null, g_year)

yrs <- data.frame(year = factor(levels(stations$year), levels = levels(stations$year)))
pc <- predict(g_year, newdata = yrs, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
yrs$prob <- plogis(pc$fit)
yrs$lwr <- plogis(pc$fit - 1.96 * pc$se.fit)
yrs$upr <- plogis(pc$fit + 1.96 * pc$se.fit)
yrs

# the easy way: the same numbers in one line
emmeans(g_year, ~ year, type = "response")
```

## Your turn, in biology {.smaller}

Highly susceptible corals were recorded at about a quarter of Tortugas stations
in 2016 and 2018, fewer in 2021, the year the disease arrived, and at
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * yrs$prob[4])` in 2022. The year model beats a single
constant probability by `r sprintf("%.1f", AIC(g_null) - AIC(g_year))` AIC
units.

## For anyone fast: a control {.smaller}

```{r}
others <- corals$station[grepl("Siderastrea|Montastraea|Porites", corals$COVER_CAT_NAME)]
stations$other <- as.numeric(stations$station %in% others)
tapply(stations$other, stations$year, mean)

g_other <- glm(other ~ year, family = binomial, data = stations)
exp(coef(g_other)["year2022"])      # odds in 2022 relative to 2016
exp(coef(g_year)["year2022"])       # the same for susceptible corals
```

Less susceptible corals dip in 2021 and mostly recover; the susceptible ones
fall by far more. The survey design changed in 2021, so a drop in everything
would have been hard to read; a drop in only the susceptible species points at
the disease.
